fix: Borrow instead of cloning: `if let Some(decoration) = &self.material_decoration {`. `InputDecoration::apply_defaults` takes `&self` and already returns an owned copy (see input.rs:664), so the clone on this line is a second, redundant whole-struct clone on every build.

Use the borrowing accessor: `.empty(self.controller.with_value(|value| value.text.is_empty()))`. `text()` clones the entire editor string only to test emptiness; the same clone is repeated at line 818 for the semantics value (keep that one, it needs an owned String).

Consume the values instead of cloning: `let decoration = match validation_error { Some(error) => decoration.error(error), None => decoration };`. The current `map_or` eagerly clones the whole InputDecoration even when there is no validation error, and clones the error string needlessly.

Change the helper to borrow: `fn label_text(&self) -> Option<&str> { self.semantic_label.as_deref() }`, use `self.label_text().is_some()` as-is, and at line 793 use `Text::new(label)` (Text::new takes impl Into<String>, so &str works). This removes a String clone per presence check and per use.

Replace the loop with one call: `field = field.input_formatters(value.input_formatters);`. `TextField::input_formatters` accepts `impl IntoIterator<Item = Rc<dyn TextInputFormatter>>` (text_fields.rs:592), and the order is preserved.

Drop the debug_assert here and at line 184 (CupertinoDesktopTextSelectionToolbar::new). Handle empty input in the `From` impls the way AdaptiveTextSelectionToolbar already does (text_selection_toolbar.rs:375): `if value.children.is_empty() { return SizedBox::shrink().into(); }` before building. Public constructors then never panic on app-author input.
Borrow the stored text: `Text::new(value.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default())`. Text::new takes impl Into<String>, so the &str works and the Option<String> clone is avoided.
